That is the elder (of her twins) should serve the younger. Secondly, holic Scripture testifieth in the same chapter (v. 27.) That perceiuing at last Gods will, that Jacob should be preferred, was neither offended with him nor revoked his blessing as unlawfully surprised, but condescending thereto, ratified that he had done, saying (v. 33.) I have blessed him, and he shall be bleſſed. Sixtly, God himself from this time forwards often appeared to Jacob, and with great promises and manie temporal and spiritual benefits, declared his singular loue to him. Seuenthly, the three Patriarcharchs, Abraham, Isaac, & Jacob, are special renowned Saints of the old Testament: yea the Lord and Creator of all would peculiarly be called (Exodi 3.) the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. Moyses praying instantly for Gods mercie and clemencie towards the people (Exodi 32.) besought him to remember Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, his servants: and so in both old and new Testament these three are often mentioned as chiefe Princes in the Kingdomome of Heaven. Al which shew the great vertues and holiness of them all.
